facts.text: Three distinct but interlocking literatures govern professional relationships. Trust is dyadic willingness to be vulnerable. Rapport is the moment-to-moment relational tone. Psychological safety is a group-level climate belief. They are not the same thing - build all three deliberately.
This skill is about trust between people. For trust in machines/automation (over-reliance, algorithm aversion, calibration), use human-ai-interaction-psychology.
Meta-finding across all three: trust and safety are slow to build and fast to destroy (Slovic). Match every move to that asymmetry.
Deep detail, the repair decision aid, the full 7-item scale, and source citations live in references/trust-rapport-safety-detail.md. Load it when you need specifics.
See the 6-step repair decision aid in the reference file.

Safety is NOT niceness. Pair high safety with high accountability/standards (Edmondson's learning zone). Never sell it as "be nice." And trust is NOT blindness - mature trust is calibrated by evidence.
Edmondson 7-item exact wording varies across secondary reproductions; the version in refs is the most common, but verify against the 1999 ASQ original before any formal measurement.

Team positive:negative ratio - the marital 5:1 is well replicated; the team threshold rests partly on Losada's math, later critiqued (Brown, Sokal & Friedman 2013). The direction (high performers run positive-heavy) holds; treat a specific team number as heuristic, not law.
